episode_title: BREAKING: October LSAT Scores Are Out

real_qa.q: What is the LSAT Score Preview window and deadline for October 2024 test takers?
real_qa.r: Test takers with Score Preview have six days from score release to decide whether to keep or cancel their score. Once scores are released, if you don't take action within those six days, your score is automatically reported to law schools. The deadline for October LSAT scores is approximately November 3rd. Cancellation is final and counts toward your lifetime limit of seven LSATs.

real_qa.q: What LSAT score range puts you in the top scholarship money tier at law schools?
real_qa.r: A score of 160 and above is where you start getting meaningful scholarship money. At schools with medians of 170 or higher, 6.6% of the class receives a full ride or better, the highest rate on the scale. A score of 165 puts you in the 85th percentile and above the median at three-quarters of law schools. Employment rates in the 165-169 band reach 94.4%, and at 170 plus schools, employment is 96.9%.

real_qa.q: How many law schools now have a median LSAT of 160 or higher compared to 2015?
real_qa.r: In 2015, 49 law schools had a median LSAT of 160 or higher. As of the 2025 ABA filings, 91 law schools now report a median of 160 or higher, representing nearly a doubling of schools at that threshold. The floor of the market has risen significantly, with only eight schools now reporting a median below 150, down from 45 schools in 2015.

real_qa.q: What is the employment rate for law school graduates scoring in different LSAT ranges?
real_qa.r: Employment rates vary significantly by LSAT score range. At schools with medians below 150, only 53.1% of 2025 graduates got full-time long-term jobs requiring or preferring a JD. In the 150-154 band, that rises to 77.3%. At 155-159, it reaches 85.1%. In the 160-164 range, employment clears 90% at 90.1%. At 165-169, employment is 94.4%, and at 170 plus schools, it reaches 96.9%.
real_qa.requete: LSAT score employment rate by range

real_qa.q: How did the LSAC percentile table change and what does this mean for current test takers?
real_qa.r: LSAC updated its percentile table without major announcement, causing score conversions to shift downward. A 170 now sits at the 94.5th percentile, where a 169 used to sit; a 165 now equals what a 164 was previously. Under the older table, 4.4% of test takers scored 170 or higher, but on the current table, it is 5.5%—25% more people competing at the top. This means test takers rank lower relative to others with the same numerical score.

guest.bio_context: Steve Schwartz improved his own LSAT score from 152 to 175 and has been coaching the LSAT since 2005. He provides guidance on test strategy, score interpretation, and law school admissions decisions based on published ABA data.

real_quote: If you're above the median, schools will start chasing you, and that's where you can get real scholarship money, maybe even a full ride, maybe even a full ride with a stipend.
